# Instant hero backdrop

## Glossary

* **Hero backdrop** — the full-viewport backdrop image behind the Home page
  hero (`.page-backdrop` in `HomeLive`). The Library and Incoming header
  bands (`.page-atmosphere`) draw from the same pool and the same serving
  path; "hero backdrop" covers all three unless a phase says otherwise.
* **Master** — the original TMDB artwork file on disk. Backdrops are fetched
  at TMDB `original`, typically 3000–3840 px wide.
* **Derivative** — a width-bounded copy of a master generated by
  `MediaCentaur.ImageFiles.derivative/2` and requested with `?w=<px>`.
  The hero backdrop is the one surface that renders the master
  (`sized_image_url/2` with `:full_bleed`).
* **Live navigation** — a LiveView `navigate` between pages. The root layout
  and `app.js` survive it; the page DOM, including every `<img>`, is
  destroyed and rebuilt.
* **Sync decode** — `decoding="sync"` on in-flow images, mandated by
  UIDR-012 and enforced by MC0016: the frame waits for the decode so the
  page never paints a blank slot.
* **Decoded-bitmap cache** — the JavaScript-owned cache of `ImageBitmap`
  objects keyed by image URL (`assets/js/hooks/hero_backdrop.js`). It
  survives live navigation because it lives in `app.js`, not in the page DOM.
* **Media-center shell** — the dedicated browser instance that runs the
  app on the TV. Launched by `~/scripts/media-centaur/run` (outside this
  repo, not in dotfiles): a `--app` window, dedicated profile,
  XWayland for a stable window class, occlusion throttling disabled.

## Goal

Make the Home hero backdrop appear in the same frame the page mounts,
every time, at the master's full resolution. Before this campaign every
return to Home re-decoded a 3840×2160 JPEG and the backdrop visibly filled
in after the rest of the page; it was the one place in the app that read as
unstable. The owner declined trading pixels for speed, so the fix had to
keep the look untouched.

## Status

Phase 1 done and verified except for physical input (owner check). Phase 2
measured, prototyped, measured again, and **adopted** as [UIDR-032](../decisions/user-interface/2026-09-06-032-page-hero-backdrops-paint-from-a-decoded-bitmap-cache.md),
shipped as **v1.14.0** on 2026-09-07. The dev server and the shell are running
the new code.

### Baseline (media-center shell, Chromium 152, GPU raster, 2026-09-06)

Walk: Home → Discovery → Incoming → Status → Settings → Library (scroll the
grid end to end, decode 60 unseen derivatives) → Home. Five returns.

| Measure | `<img>` hero (before) | canvas + bitmap cache (after) |
|---|---|---|
| hero decode task on return (trace, `ImageDecodeTask`) | 4 of 5 returns; 32–50 ms, median 46 ms | none |
| hero present in the first frame after the click | no: page painted without it at ~90 ms, bands at ~200 ms, complete at ~240 ms | yes, every return (first frame 57–116 ms after the click, which is the LiveView round trip) |
| element inserted → hero painted | not measurable for `<img>` (Element Timing did not fire for the rebuilt element) | 0 ms, same task as the DOM patch |
| renderer RSS with the cache full (3 bitmaps) | — | 327 MB main renderer, 301 MB GPU process |

Why the rapid first walk without pressure looked fine: re-walking pages the
GPU image cache has already seen adds nothing, so nothing evicts the hero.
Browsing new artwork between visits is what evicts it, and that is normal use.

Earlier dev-server numbers (headless, software raster) that framed the work:
master decode ~50 ms vs ~8 ms for a 1920 derivative; Home decodes 51 images,
22.7 MP, ~70 ms in total besides the hero; 43 hero-candidate masters:
12 × 3840, 16 × 3360, 1 × 3000, 11 × 1920, 3 × 1280.

## Decisions made

* `2026-09-06` — **Bounded derivative declined.** Rendering the hero at
  1920 or a new 2560 rung removes most of the decode cost but upscales
  29 of 43 hero masters on the 4K panel. Owner wants the look untouched.
* `2026-09-06` — **Format change declined.** Baseline JPEG is already the
  cheapest mainstream format to decode; WebP is no better, AVIF is several
  times worse. Re-encoding the master at 4:2:0 would save roughly a third
  of the decode and still leave a visible pop. Not pursued.
* `2026-09-06` — **Browser switch is housekeeping, not a fix.** Vivaldi
  and Chromium share the engine; the hero behaves identically in both.
  Switching removes Vivaldi's three idle extension processes and tracks
  upstream sooner. It also gives Phase 2 a plain Chromium to profile.
* `2026-09-06` — **Shell switched to Chromium 152.0.7977.75** (Phase 1).
  Launcher edited in place, previous launcher kept as
  `~/scripts/media-centaur/run.vivaldi-backup`, profile
  `~/.config/chromium-mediacenter`, loopback DevTools on :9222.
* `2026-09-06` — **Chromium does not honour `decoding="sync"` for the 4K
  hero on the GPU raster path.** Screencast frames show the page painted
  with the hero region empty, then the picture rastered in bands. This is
  the exact visual the owner reported. Answered the campaign's first open
  question.
* `2026-09-07` — **Decoded-bitmap cache adopted** ([UIDR-032](../decisions/user-interface/2026-09-06-032-page-hero-backdrops-paint-from-a-decoded-bitmap-cache.md)).
  `Components.HeroBackdrop` (canvas + `HeroBackdrop` hook) replaces the
  `<img>` on Home, Library, and Incoming; `LiveHelpers.hero_backdrop_src/1`
  is the one URL function on both sides; `ArtworkWarmup.hero_backdrop_urls/0`
  marks the prefetch hints `data-hero-backdrop` and `app.js` pre-decodes them
  at idle. Miss path: draw when decoded, never block. Canvas output matches
  the image in composition, position, and colour (frame comparison).
* `2026-09-07` — **Sticky-element alternative declined** for good: the
  bitmap cache gives the same result without touching page layout.
* `2026-09-07` — **Shipped v1.14.0** (tag `v1.14.0`, changelog entry under
  *Improved*). Owner ran `/ship minor` after reviewing the overnight work.

## Next steps

1. **Owner, in the morning:** confirm arrow keys, gamepad, and the FLIRC
   remote's four buttons drive the Chromium shell as they did Vivaldi. Every
   automated check passed (window class `media-centaur` on XWayland, second
   launch focuses instead of duplicating, socket alive after 60 s under
   fullscreen mpv, `document.hasFocus()` true after launch), but physical
   input cannot be verified from a script.
2. Owner: look at Home, Library, and Incoming on the TV and confirm the hero
   reads exactly as before. Then browse a few pages and return to Home — the
   backdrop should be there in the first frame.
3. Once satisfied: delete `~/.config/vivaldi-mediacenter` and
   `~/scripts/media-centaur/run.vivaldi-backup`. (Shipped v1.14.0 already.)
4. Close the campaign (remove this file; git history is the archive).

## Completion criteria

* The media-center shell runs Chromium with the launcher contract verified
  (class detection, no duplicates, socket survives mpv occlusion, remote and
  gamepad input work). **Remaining: remote and gamepad, owner check.**
* A Phase 2 decision is recorded with before/after medians from the real
  shell, whichever way it goes. **Done.**
* If adopted: Home, Library, and Incoming hero backdrops paint in the mount
  frame on return, at master resolution, with tests and the UIDR landed.
  **Done** (bun tests on the cache and hook; LiveView tests on the three hosts;
  warmup-key agreement test; UIDR-032).
* The Vivaldi media-center profile is removed. **Remaining, after the owner
  check.**

## Pointers

* Serving path: `MediaCentaurWeb.Plugs.ImageServer`,
  `MediaCentaur.ImageFiles.derivative/2` (ladder tops out at 1920),
  `MediaCentaurWeb.LiveHelpers.sized_image_url/2`, `hero_backdrop_src/1`.
* Hero selection and warmup: `MediaCentaurWeb.HomeLive.Logic.select_page_hero/3`,
  `MediaCentaurWeb.ArtworkWarmup`, root layout prefetch block.
* The cache and hook: `assets/js/hooks/hero_backdrop.js` (+ bun test),
  `MediaCentaurWeb.Components.HeroBackdrop`.
* Rendering policy: [UIDR-012](../decisions/user-interface/2026-05-20-012-desktop-app-rendering-defaults.md),
  [UIDR-032](../decisions/user-interface/2026-09-06-032-page-hero-backdrops-paint-from-a-decoded-bitmap-cache.md),
  Credo `MC0016`, `MC0028`.
* Launcher: `~/scripts/media-centaur/run`; window-class notes in
  `~/knowledge/hyprland/chromium-window-class.md`.
* Measuring the real shell: attach to `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json` with
  `~/scripts/agents/_cdp.js` (`cdpClient`, `evaluate`). The method that
  produced the table: inject a `MutationObserver` that timestamps the hero
  element's insertion and (for the canvas) its `data-hero-state="drawn"`
  flip; `Tracing.start` with `blink,cc,devtools.timeline` and sum
  `ImageDecodeTask` durations; `Page.startScreencast` and measure the mean
  luminance of the hero's unobscured upper-right region per frame. Apply
  cache pressure between returns or the hero never gets evicted. Dev static
  assets carry `max-age=3600`, so after `mix assets.build` the shell needs a
  cache-clearing reload (`Network.clearBrowserCache` + `Page.reload`).
* Post-ship incident (2026-09-07): the dev app died after the release because
  the `live_reload` regexes in `config/dev.exs` carried per-VM references
  (OTP 28+), so Mix judged the app config "changed" on every cross-process
  compile and force-rebuilt every dependency and module; a hot rebuild that
  long leaves the running app without its modules. Fixed by moving that block
  to `config/runtime.exs`, and `scripts/ship release` now restarts the dev
  service after the version bump. The earlier note here blaming the code
  reloader for "only reloading what it compiled itself" was wrong.
* Headless: `~/scripts/agents/chromium-probe` (no window focus, transitions
  never settle — assert on state, not on animated values).
